subject: Oceanography
title: The Solubility Pump
description: A 60-second lesson on The Solubility Pump.

hook.text: Cold water dissolves more CO₂ than warm water—so polar oceans inhale carbon while tropical oceans exhale it.

buildup.text: At high latitudes, cold surface water absorbs CO₂ from the air—then sinks, carrying that carbon deep.

discovery.text: This solubility pump accounts for most of the ocean's CO₂ uptake—physics doing what biology can't alone.

twist.text: As oceans warm, their ability to dissolve CO₂ decreases—a warming ocean absorbs less carbon.

climax.text: This positive feedback could accelerate warming—less absorption means more CO₂ stays in the atmosphere.

punchline.text: The colder the water, the more carbon it swallows—warming weakens the appetite.

quiz.question: Why do polar oceans absorb more CO₂?
options: Cold water dissolves more CO₂ than warm water
